title: A simplified protocol for MAGMA/H-MAGMA gene set analysis using high-performance computing
author: Zhang

steps.title: Set up software environment
steps.instruction: Install a Unix‑like operating system (Linux ≥ Fedora 19/Debian 7, macOS 10.10+, or Ubuntu 20.04 LTS on Windows 10). Create a Python virtual environment with venv, Miniconda, or Anaconda. Install GNU Parallel. Download MAGMA and H‑MAGMA from the distributor sites listed in the key‑resource table. (Optional) Install R > 4.0 with libraries readr > 1.3.1, ggplot2 > 3.3.0, and RColorBrewer > 1.1 for plotting.

substeps.instruction: Verify OS version meets requirements.
Create and activate a Python virtual environment.
Run `conda install -c conda-forge parallel` or equivalent to install GNU Parallel.
Download the MAGMA binary and the H‑MAGMA annotation package from the official website.
If plotting is desired, install R and the required packages.

steps.title: Prepare input data files
steps.instruction: Gather the genomic‑interval list(s) or peak files from your differential expression or ChIP‑seq analysis, ensuring they use the same genome build as the GWAS (typically GRCh37/hg19). Obtain the SNP‑p‑value file (e.g., PGC 3 Schizophrenia wave 3 TSV) and the gene annotation file (standard or H‑MAGMA) that matches your cell‑type of interest.

substeps.instruction: Confirm genome version consistency between interval files and GWAS association files.
Place the SNP‑p‑value file (e.g., `PGC3_SCZ_wave3_public.2021.v2.tsv`) in an accessible directory.
Place the gene annotation file (e.g., `miR137_100k_20k.genes.annot`) in an accessible directory.

steps.title: Check system CPU and memory
steps.instruction: Determine available computational resources. In a terminal run `lscpu | grep "CPU"` to note the number of logical CPUs/threads. Then run `free -h` to see total usable memory (GiB).

substeps.instruction: Record the number of logical CPUs (e.g., 64).
Record the total memory (e.g., 458 GiB).

steps.title: Determine parallel thread count
steps.instruction: Calculate the maximum number of parallel MAGMA threads: each thread uses ~1 GiB of RAM, so max threads = floor(available GiB / 1). Do not exceed the number of logical CPUs. Reserve resources for the OS and cap threads at 10 if the machine has < 16 logical cores, or at 40 for larger clusters, provided memory permits.

substeps.instruction: Compute `max_threads = min(floor(memory_GiB), logical_CPUs)`.
Apply the cap: if logical_CPUs < 16, set `threads = min(max_threads, 10)`; otherwise `threads = min(max_threads, 40)`.

steps.title: Create gene analysis script
steps.instruction: Make a temporary directory and write a Bash script (`gene_analysis.sh`) containing the MAGMA parallel command. Replace placeholder paths with your actual file locations and set `Output_Prefix` as desired.

substeps.instruction: Run `mkdir temp_annot` to create a folder for intermediate files.
Create `gene_analysis.sh` with the following content (adjust paths):

#!/bin/bash
mkdir temp_annot
Data_File="/data/your-name/magma/aux-files/g1000_eur"
Annot_File="miR137_100k_20k.genes.annot"
SNP_Pval_File="/data/your-name/PGC3/PGC3_SCZ_wave3_public.2021.v2.tsv"
Output_Prefix="miR137_PGC_SCZ_w3"
parallel magma \ 
  --batch {} $threads \ 
  --bfile $Data_File \ 
  --gene-annot $Annot_File \ 
  --gene-model snp-wise=mean \ 
  --pval $SNP_Pval_File ncol=Nca \ 
  --out temp_annot/$Output_Prefix \ 
  ::: {1..$threads}

magma \ 
  --merge temp_annot/$Output_Prefix \ 
  --out temp_annot/$Output_Prefix

cp temp_annot/$Output_Prefix.genes.* .
rm -r temp_annot
Save and close the file.

steps.title: Run gene analysis
steps.instruction: Make the script executable (optional) and execute it to produce `.genes.raw`, `.genes.out`, and `.log` files.

substeps.instruction: Run `chmod +x gene_analysis.sh` (optional).
Execute `bash ./gene_analysis.sh`.
Verify that files `miR137_PGC_SCZ_w3.genes.raw`, `miR137_PGC_SCZ_w3.genes.out`, and `miR137_PGC_SCZ_w3.log` appear.

steps.title: Specify sample size for p-values
steps.instruction: Inspect the header of the SNP‑p‑value file to identify the sample‑size column name (e.g., `Nca`, `Neff`, `Ngt`). If the column is absent, obtain the sample size from the accompanying README and plan to use `N = <value>` in the MAGMA command instead of `ncol`.

substeps.instruction: Open the SNP‑p‑value TSV file and view the first line.
Note the column name that contains the effective sample size.
If missing, locate the sample size in the README and record it (e.g., N = 25350).

steps.title: Select appropriate annotation file
steps.instruction: If performing H‑MAGMA, replace the standard `Annot_File` with the H‑MAGMA cell‑type‑specific annotation provided by the H‑MAGMA package; otherwise keep the standard annotation used in step 5.

steps.title: Create gene set annotation file
steps.instruction: Prepare a gene‑set list file (`Set_Annot_File`) in column‑based format (column 2 = gene ID, column 1 = set name). Use ENSEMBL IDs without version suffixes (e.g., `ENSG00000153266`). Ensure each line ends with a Unix newline (`\n`) only, not Windows carriage return (`\r\n`).

substeps.instruction: Write the file in a text editor or export from Excel and strip `\r` characters.
Save as, for example, `miR137_gene_set_list_4_magma.txt`.

steps.title: Create gene set analysis script
steps.instruction: Write a Bash script (`gene_set_analysis.sh`) that calls MAGMA with the gene‑level results and the gene‑set annotation file.

substeps.instruction: Create `gene_set_analysis.sh` with the following content (adjust paths):

#!/bin/bash
Gene_Results_File="miR137_PGC_SCZ_w3.genes.raw"
Set_Annot_File="/data/your-name/analysis-results/miR137_gene_set_list_4_magma.txt"
Output_Prefix="miR137_100k_20k_gene_set_results"

magma \ 
  --gene-results $Gene_Results_File \ 
  --set-annot $Set_Annot_File col=2,1 \ 
  --out $Output_Prefix
Save and close the file.

steps.title: Run gene set analysis
steps.instruction: Execute the gene‑set script to generate the `.gsa.out` results file.

substeps.instruction: Run `chmod +x gene_set_analysis.sh` (optional).
Execute `bash ./gene_set_analysis.sh`.
Confirm creation of `miR137_100k_20k_gene_set_results.gsa.out`.

steps.title: Optional: Plot results in R
steps.instruction: Generate bubble‑plot visualizations of beta coefficients and -log10 P values using R. Install required packages, create an R script with the provided code, and run it in RStudio.

substeps.instruction: In R, install packages: `install.packages(c('readr','ggplot2','RColorBrewer'))`.
Create an R script (e.g., `plot_gsa.R`) containing:

# init
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(RColorBrewer)

df_raw <- read_table2("Apr122021_set_analysis.gsa.out", skip = 4)
df_raw$`-log10P` <- -log10(df_raw$P)
df_raw$VARIABLE <- factor(df_raw$VARIABLE, levels = c('Glut','NPC','DA','GABA','iPS'))
df_raw$TYPE <- 'PGC_SCZ_w3'

ggplot(df_raw, aes(x = VARIABLE, y = TYPE, size = BETA, fill = `-log10P`)) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = 'white', high = 'darkred', limits = c(0,7)) +
  scale_size_area(limits = c(0,0.5)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21) +
  xlab('Cell type') + ylab('') +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = 'bottom', legend.box = 'horizontal',
        axis.text = element_text(size = 14), axis.title = element_text(size = 16))
Open the script in RStudio, select all, and press Ctrl+Enter (or run line‑by‑line).
The bubble plot will appear in the RStudio Plots pane.
